newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK C.BANK SEES CROWN SEEN STABLE IN NEAR TERM.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK C.BANK SEES CROWN SEEN STABLE IN NEAR TERM.

text.p: A devaluation of the Slovak crown in the near future is not probable, and strong foreign currency reserves should help it remain stable, a senior central bank official said on Monday.

"The situation is not dramatic, our foreign exchange reserves are stable and are big enough to cover the potential needs of domestic banks," Juraj Janosik, head of the NBS banking transactions division, told a conference on Monday.
He added that foreign currency reserves currently are sufficient to cover 3.7 to 3.8 months of imports as well as to maintain current exchange rates.

The central bank on Monday fixed the crown at 30.894 to the dollar after Friday's fixing at 30.954, and at 20.532 to the mark from 20.502. The rates imply a deviation from the crown's currency basket midpoint of -0.50 percent, after a deviation of -0.49 percent on Friday.
The trade deficit hit 37.2 billion crowns for the first nine months of the year, after recording a 405 million crown surplus over the same period last year.

In a monthly investor report, bank ING Barings echoed Janosik's words on currency stability, saying favourable trends in the growth of the money supply should help ease any pressures brought about by the deficit.
"In coming months, growth in the money supply is expected to slow, resulting in reduced imports and a decrease in the pace of trade deficit growth," the ING report said.

The report said devaluation would not resolve the trade problem as it would only influence the general level of prices since the decline in exports was caused mainly by a lower economic growth in Slovakia's main trade partners.

The plus-minus five percent daily fixing fluctuation band of the crown and the present policy of the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) are sufficient to maintain a stable exchange rates, the report said.
"However the NBS will have to closely watch labour productivity increases...in order to maintain stable exchange rate," it said.
